https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/articles/cwym.text: Image source, Telegram/Crimeanwind Image caption, Huge plumes of smoke seen rising in the skies from the site where the Slavneft-Yanos oil refinery in Russia is located By Jaroslav Lukiv Published 6 August 2026, 12:35 BST Updated 1 hour ago Ukraine said it has hit two oil refineries in multiple strikes deep inside Russia with patrol boats and other vessels in the Black Sea also hit. President Volodymyr Zelensky said the Bashneft-Novoil and Slavneft-Yanos refineries were struck in the attacks aimed at limiting oil revenues Moscow "uses to finance" its war. Yaroslavl regional governor Mikhail Evraev said Slavneft-Yanos was on fire after what he called the "largest enemy drone attack". He said four people were injured. Meanwhile, Ukraine said at least 11 people were killed in Russian attacks, and the southern city of Kherson reported a total blackout. Russia said it targeted fuel, energy and transport facilities. In Odesa, no-one is safe from Russia's new Black Sea strikes Published 8 hours ago After deadly Kyiv strike, Ukraine warns interceptor shortage is costing lives Published 19 hours ago Both Russia and Ukraine have in recent weeks intensified attacks on major cities, energy facilities and warehouses, as the vast front line remains virtually static and all mediation efforts to end the war have brought no breakthrough. Russian President Vladimir Putin launched a full-scale invasion of Ukraine in February 2022. Zelensky said on Thursday that the struck Bashneft-Novoil refinery in Russia's Bashkortostan republic was about 1,300km (808 miles) from the Ukrainian border, whereas Slavneft-Yanos was almost 700km (435 miles) away. The Ukrainian president also said that "two military patrol boats and shadow fleet vessels were hit" in the Black Sea, referring to tankers used by Russia to illegally export sanctioned oil. "Russia must choose peace," Zelensky said, adding that Ukrainian attacks were "strengthening chances for diplomacy". Evraev said 93 drones were shot down over Yaroslavl region overnight. "Falling debris hit the oil refinery's storage tanks. Emergency services are working to extinguish the fire," he said. BBC Verify confirmed multiple videos and images shared on social media showing huge smoke plumes rising from the refinery. In one of the verified images there appear to be at least four fires at the site. Energy-generating infrastructure in Yaroslavl has been targeted a number of times by Ukraine. The authorities in Bashkortostan have not publicly commented on the reported Ukrainian attack on the Bashneft-Novoil refinery on 5 August. Image source, DSNS Ukraine Image caption, Private residential houses were hit in Russia's overnight drone attack on Ukraine's north-eastern town of Balakliya, local officials said In Ukraine, three people were killed in the town of Balakliya, Kharkiv region, in an overnight Russian drone attack, the country's state emergencies service DSNS said. It said private residential houses were targeted, with fires reported in two buildings. Kharkiv regional head Oleh Synehubov later said that another two people were killed when drones attacked the train station in Lozova. Another eight people were injured. Later on Thursday, five people were killed in Russian strikes on the central Dnipropetrovsk region, local officials said. In the south, the entire city of Kherson is now without electricity after a "critical infrastructure facility" was hit overnight, regional head Oleksandr Prokudin said. In Ukraine's Black Sea port of Odesa, one person was killed when Russia hit two dry cargo ships. Meanwhile, the Russian military said its forces intercepted or shot down 605 Ukrainian drones overnight over a number of regions. In its latest operational update, the military said it struck Ukraine's fuel, energy and transport facilities, as well as drone storage sites. http://www.chinanationalnews.com/news/27.text: Revolut handed sensitive customer data to scammers media RT.com 13 Sep 2026, 03:02 GMT+10 The UK-based digital bank reportedly disclosed sensitive customer information after receiving requests from a government agency email domain London-based fintech company Revolut disclosed sensitive customer information to scammers after receiving fraudulent requests sent from a "legitimate government agency email domain," according to media reports on Saturday. The exposed data included customers' birth dates, phone numbers, postal and email addresses, as well as copies of passports and driver's licenses, according to a notification Revolut sent to affected clients and cited by the online newspaper TechCrunch. The compromised data may also have included verification selfies, account statements, and transaction histories, according to the report. Revolut confirmed the breach to both TechCrunch and Reuters, saying a "limited" number of customers had been affected by a "sophisticated external impersonation scam where an unauthorized third party utilized a legitimate government agency domain email to submit fraudulent requests for information." Co-founded by Russian-born entrepreneur Nik Storonsky in 2015, Revolut describes itself as the "world's first truly global bank," which provides digital banking services to more than 80 million customers worldwide. The incident comes as Revolut has been rapidly expanding internationally. A little over a month ago, it was granted a banking license in France, while the company has also been expanding its presence in markets including India, Mexico, and the UAE. Last week, the US Office of the Comptroller of the Currency issued a conditional approval to Revolut, allowing it to set up a bank in the country. Late last month, police on the British island of Jersey warned Revolut users of an uptick in fraud cases, where the victims had received a telephone call from scammers posing as Revolut support or security teams. Several countries have also taken issue with the company's practices in recent years. In April, Italian authorities slapped the online bank with fines totaling €11.5 million ($13.25 million) over alleged unfair commercial practices. Last year, the central bank of Lithuania fined Revolut €3.5 million, accusing it of failing to comply with money laundering prevention regulations. https://www.henricocitizen.com/henrico-s.text: Education — Henrico School Board — Henrico County Public Schools — Amy Cashwell — Varina Center for Environmental Studies and Sustainability — Living Building Henrico School Board to discuss Living Building delay, launch naming process Sept. 24 , and Tom Lappas, Citizen Publisher September 18, 2026 . 1:35 PM 3 min read 𝕏 Share on Facebook Share on Pinterest Share on LinkedIn Share on WhatsApp Share via Email A rendering of the planned Living Building in Varina, which will house the Varina Center for Environmental Studies and Sustainability (Courtesy Henrico Schools) The Henrico School Board will hold a work session and monthly meeting Sept. 24, with an update on the county's new environmental education facility, the start of a public process to name the building and several grant awards among the items scheduled for consideration. The work session will begin at 4 p.m. at the New Bridge Learning Center Auditorium, 5915 Nine Mile Road. The monthly meeting will follow at 6:30 p.m. at the same location. Perhaps the most significant update will come during the work session, when school officials are scheduled to brief board members about the division's new environmental education Living Building, now under construction. The project has fallen behind its previous construction schedule. Substantial completion originally was targeted for winter 2026-27, but construction delays have pushed that milestone to spring 2027, according to the presentation prepared for the board. HCPS now expects the facility to open in fall 2027. The building will house the Varina Center for Environmental Studies and Sustainability and also provide environmental-learning opportunities for students from throughout Henrico. Two new VCESS courses – Introduction to Plant Systems and a Senior Internship – will give students roles in programming at the building. The plant-systems course will support third-grade agriculture and plant-based learning, while students in the internship will help support programming for third- and sixth-graders alongside environmental educators. The School Board also is scheduled to launch a 30-day public-comment period to select a permanent name for the facility. A steering committee includes VCESS students, HEART Youth Council representatives, educators, Varina High School alumni, ministers from the Varina community, a Varina resident and biologist and representatives of the Henricopolis Soil and Water Conservation District, among others. The comment period is scheduled to begin Sept. 24 and end Oct. 25. Superintendent Amy Cashwell then is scheduled to present recommendations Nov. 12, when the board is expected to act on the building's name. HEF Greenlight grants earmarked for 12 school projects During the 6:30 p.m. monthly meeting, board members will consider accepting $76,545 in Henrico Education Foundation Greenlight grants supporting 12 projects – nine at elementary schools and three at high schools. School officials estimate the projects collectively will affect more than 9,300 students, teachers and parents. The largest award, $14,000, would support the Dolphin Discovery Trail at Donahoe Elementary School, an outdoor-learning project designed to expand hands-on science instruction. Other awards include $11,000 to expand the division's Go ALL IN initiative; $10,412 for a literacy-based “Curiosity Classroom” project involving Colonial Trail and Nuckols Farm elementary schools; and $9,536 for a career-exploration program at Longan Elementary. Varina High School would receive $6,065 for a yearlong Blue Devil Film Festival program through which students would develop, produce and publicly screen original short films. Dumbarton Elementary would receive $6,500 for a before-school enrichment program incorporating robotics, esports, arts and wellness activities. Other grants also likely to be accepted Two other grant awards are scheduled for consideration. A $7,500 award from the Propane Education and Research Council would allow the ACE Center at Virginia Randolph to incorporate propane-vehicle inspection training into its diesel-technology curriculum. About 40 juniors and seniors are expected to participate. The board also will consider accepting a $48,335.08 Virginia Department of Education grant for the Individual Student Alternative Education Plan program. The program serves students 16 and older who are at least one full year behind in credits and at risk of not graduating on time. Approximately 40 students are expected to participate this year, receiving services that include GED preparation, economics and personal-finance instruction and career and technical education. Other items, public comment opportunities Board members also will receive the school division's financial reports through Aug. 31. The amended FY2027 general-fund budget reflects a $6.1 million supplemental appropriation from Henrico County associated with the 4% wage increase for returning HCPS employees. The consent agenda also includes permanent and temporary easements for a new underground sanitary-sewer system serving the rebuilt Quioccasin Middle School. The permanent easement encompasses 3,028 square feet, while two temporary construction easements total 3,591 square feet. The monthly meeting will open with a performance by the Glen Allen High School Drumline and include recognition of HCPS programs that earned 2026 National Association of Counties Achievement Awards. The board also is scheduled to recognize October as National Bullying Prevention Month and National Czech, Italian and Polish Heritage Month. The monthly meeting includes a public-comment period. People wishing to speak in person must register in advance through HCPS or contact the School Board clerk by 4:30 p.m. Sept. 23; written comments must be submitted by noon Sept. 23. https://telex.hu/ellenorzo/2026/10/18/cs.text: Menü Kereső Fact-check: Tényleg Magyar Péter és a Tisza Párt miatt születik kevesebb gyerek, ahogy Takács Péter állítja? Ellenőrző Bakró-Nagy Ferenc Állítsd be a Telexet megbízható forrásnak! Beállítom Takács Péter, a Fidesz-kormány egykori egészségügyi államtitkára egy hete arról beszélt, hogy Magyar Péter és a Tisza Párt tehet arról, hogy 2025-ben csökkent a gyerekszületések száma . A volt államtitkár, jelenlegi országgyűlési képviselő a Digitális Polgári Körök (DPK) első országos táborában tartott, a YouTube-on is közzétett beszélgetésen úgy fogalmazott, hogy a romlás 2024 nyarán következett be, ennek oka a Tisza Párt és Magyar Péter. Takács Péter ezt mondta: „Tehát akkor '81-től fokozatosan csökken, de így. Fidesz kormány idején egy picit sikerült ezen stabilizálni, majd így '25-ben így elkezdett leesni. Tehát van benne egy ilyen, ilyen esés. Így csökken, csökken, csökken, esik. Érdemes visszaszámolni kilenc hónapot. Merthogy ugye kilenc hónapra születik a gyerek, hogy mikor mikor születik meg a döntés arról, hogy valaki gyereket vállal, és ha visszaszámolunk kilenc hónapot, akkor a romlás az '24 nyarán következett be”, majd hozzátette: „egyetlen új tényező van '24 nyarán, egyetlenegy, a Tisza Párt és Magyar Péter”. Vajon tényleg 2024 nyarán, és tényleg a Tisza miatt zuhant be a magyarországi születésszám? A számok mást mutatnak. Mivel Takács hónapokról beszélt, az alábbi ábrán a havi adatok láthatók: a fekete görbe a tényadat, a kék pedig egy simítógörbe, hogy eltüntesse a véletlen fluktuációkat. Mint arra Ferenci Tamás biostatisztikus felhívta a figyelmet, jól látszik, hogy a nagyobb mérvű csökkenés nem 2024-ben, hanem évekkel korábban, 2021-ben kezdődött: Forrás: Ferenci Tamás / Eurostat, KSH A kérdésben megszólalt Hegedűs Zsolt egészségügyi miniszter, aki megemlítette, hogy jelentősen csökkent a gyermekvállalási korú nők száma is. A KSH 2025-ös jelentése szerint a 15–49 éves nők száma egyetlen év alatt 47 500 fővel csökkent, amiben meghatározó szerepet játszott az 1975-ben született nagy létszámú generáció kilépése ebből a korcsoportból. „Demográfiai törvényszerűség, hogy kevesebb potenciális anya mellett változatlan termékenységi gyakoriság esetén is kevesebb gyermek születik” – írta. A gyermekvállalás későbbre tolódása évtizedes demográfiai változás, vagyis a magyarországi születésszám-csökkenés hátterében több, egymással összefüggő demográfiai folyamat áll.
